title: Architecture catalog: preferred patterns and anti-patterns
maintenanceRule: A library or service SDK counts as maintained when it is not archived or deprecated and has an npm release or a default-branch commit within 12 months of verifiedAt. Fonts are judged by their distribution package, because a finished typeface needs no commits. Entries with no package and no public repository are judged by the live page alone, and say so in evidence.note.

entries.name: Monolith first, with module boundaries
entries.whenToUse: Default shape for every new project: one deployable, internal modules with explicit interfaces.
entries.avoidWhen: A hard constraint forces a separate deployable: a different runtime, isolation requirement, or scaling profile.

entries.name: Vertical slices by feature
entries.whenToUse: Organizing application code so one feature's route, logic, data access, and tests live together.
entries.avoidWhen: Shared infrastructure code (database client, auth, logging), which belongs in its own module.

entries.name: Functional core, imperative shell
entries.whenToUse: Business rules that deserve fast, exhaustive tests: keep decisions pure and push I/O to a thin shell.
entries.avoidWhen: Code that is almost all I/O glue; forcing a pure core there adds ceremony without tests worth having.

entries.name: Parse, don't validate
entries.whenToUse: Every trust boundary: turn untrusted input into a typed value once, and pass only the typed value inward.
entries.avoidWhen: Never at a trust boundary. Inside the core, do not re-check what the type already guarantees.

entries.name: Ports and adapters at external boundaries
entries.whenToUse: Each external service (payments, email, model providers): a small interface the app owns, a real adapter, and a fake for tests and the preview.
entries.avoidWhen: Internal modules and the project's own database; an interface with one implementation and no fake is speculative.

entries.name: Expand and contract (parallel change)
entries.whenToUse: Any change to a schema or interface that live code or stored data depends on: add the new shape, migrate, then remove the old shape in a later release.
entries.avoidWhen: A brand-new table or interface with no consumers and no data yet.

entries.name: Transactional outbox
entries.whenToUse: A database change must reliably trigger an external effect (email, webhook, queue message).
entries.avoidWhen: The effect is safe to lose or to run inside the request; do not add an outbox for best-effort notifications.

entries.name: Idempotency keys for retried effects
entries.whenToUse: Any operation a client, queue, or webhook may deliver more than once and that must take effect once.
entries.avoidWhen: Naturally idempotent operations such as setting a field to a value.

entries.name: Config in the environment
entries.whenToUse: Everything that differs between local, preview, and production, and every secret.
entries.avoidWhen: Constants that never vary by deploy; keep those in code.

entries.name: Strangler fig replacement
entries.whenToUse: Replacing a subsystem in an existing project: route slices to the new implementation one at a time behind a stable interface.
entries.avoidWhen: Small modules that can be replaced in one reviewed change.

entries.name: Choose boring technology
entries.whenToUse: Every technology pick: prefer what the project and the catalog already use, and justify each new moving part.
entries.avoidWhen: Never; a new technology is allowed, but only with a stated reason the boring option cannot meet.

entries.name: Microservices first
entries.whenToUse: Cite when a design splits a new or small system into separately deployed services.
entries.avoidWhen: The split is forced by a real constraint, which the decision must name.

entries.name: Building for imagined futures (YAGNI)
entries.whenToUse: Cite when a design adds extension points, config, or abstractions no acceptance criterion needs.
entries.avoidWhen: The capability is required by a criterion in this task.

entries.name: The wrong abstraction
entries.whenToUse: Cite when a design merges code paths that only look alike, or keeps bending a shared helper with flags.
entries.avoidWhen: The cases share one reason to change.

entries.name: Dual writes without atomicity
entries.whenToUse: Cite when code writes to the database and to another system in sequence and assumes both succeed.
entries.avoidWhen: The second write is best-effort by design and its loss is acceptable and stated.
